system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Buyer review — Project Kestrel

The Seller’s “STANDARD”, “FINAL” and purported prior-agreement labels are not evidence of Buyer approval. Review all positions against the AUD 24 million, debt-free/cash-free acquisition. The underlying SPA and DD documents have not been provided, so conclusions below remain subject to verification. Numerical counterproposals are Buyer negotiating positions, not assertions of market practice.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A materially higher general cap, with separate protection for fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, subject to diligence and available recourse; 20% may leave substantial acquisition risk with the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Lower thresholds, aggregation of related claims and a tipping basket; exclusions for specially protected claims. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 120,000 tipping basket**, with related claims aggregated; the Seller’s deductible structure leaves meaningful losses unrecoverable. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | General warranty claims notified within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, with longer, separate category-specific periods and workable notification requirements. | **Counter at 24 months and reject blanket application**; latent issues may emerge only through subsequent reporting cycles. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties share the general cap and time limit. | Separate capacity, authority and title protection, ordinarily capped at **100% of price**, without general thresholds, surviving for the applicable statutory period. | **Reject the general regime for fundamental warranties**; ownership and authority underpin the whole acquisition, not merely 20% of its value. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception is supplied. | Express protection for fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation, preserving available remedies and preventing contractual exclusions from shielding fraudulent conduct. | **Insert an overriding fraud carve-out across caps, thresholds, time bars, disclosure, knowledge and reliance provisions**; the Buyer must not contractually surrender fraud recourse. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of everything contained or referred to in the data room, accounts, registers and public records. | Only fair disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter, mapped to relevant warranties; a fixed, accessible disclosure archive. | **Reject blanket and “referred to” disclosure; require specific, fair disclosure and tightly defined permitted general disclosures**; document availability does not establish meaningful disclosure of a risk. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by the Buyer **or advisers**, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | No constructive or imputed knowledge exclusion; preferably no knowledge bar at all. | **Delete; fallback to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer individuals at signing**, with Seller proof and protected-category exceptions; discoverability would turn diligence into a broad waiver of warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied by delivery of written consent, although final consent and evidence addressing associated conditions are absent. | A Buyer-waivable condition requiring valid consent complying with clauses 11.2–11.3, satisfaction of associated conditions and no unacceptable adverse changes. | **Make effective consent and satisfaction of its conditions a Completion gate, with a longstop termination right**; approximately 30% of revenue is exposed and a consent document alone may not resolve the risk. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; release provided after Completion. | Verified payout figures, repayment at Completion and binding discharge/release arrangements covering all relevant security and guarantees. | **Require simultaneous payoff and effective release arrangements, with debt reflected once in the price/funds flow**; post-Completion promises do not deliver the agreed debt-free acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses treated as a Seller matter but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller economic responsibility for transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, with clear payment arrangements. | **Verify eligibility and on-costs, then expressly fund or deduct the liability without double counting, backed by an indemnity**; calling it a Seller matter does not prevent the acquired company bearing the cost. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open, without payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Verified payment and effective ownership of relevant deliverables, plus protection against associated ownership, infringement and remediation exposure. | **Require cleared-payment evidence and a confirmatory assignment at Completion; broaden the specific indemnity beyond the invoice amount**; paying a fee alone may not cure title defects or downstream loss. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, said unlikely to be material; access, scope and notification requirements remain unresolved. | Prompt investigation, evidence preservation, containment, legal notification assessment and appropriate allocation of pre-Completion incident costs and liabilities. | **Require an investigation/remediation covenant and a tailored specific indemnity, with Completion protection if findings are material**; uncertainty is not proof of either a confirmed breach or an immaterial event. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals, **AUD 330,000 aggregate**, characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Review the renewals together for timing, scope, necessity, termination rights, accrual and any departure from agreed pre-Completion conduct. | **Reserve treatment pending DD-008/DD-011 review; seek adjustment or indemnity only for identified Seller-period or unauthorised exposure**; neither ordinary-course treatment nor a full price deduction is established by the disclosure. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Explicitly separate general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, payment/completion obligations, covenants and fraud. | **Create category-specific caps, thresholds and periods with clear precedence and carve-outs**; catch-all drafting could unintentionally neutralise negotiated protections elsewhere. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Harbourglass as holder of 100% of issued shares. | Verification of issued capital, legal and beneficial ownership, encumbrances, options/conversion rights, transfer restrictions and valid transfer mechanics. | **Verify the register against supporting corporate records and searches, and require title warranties and Completion transfer deliverables**; a register entry alone does not establish clean, transferable ownership of the entire equity. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranty terms considered settled under the general regime. | A separate pre-Completion tax covenant/indemnity and tax survival period; robust IP warranties and appropriately enhanced recourse for ownership and other material IP risks. | **Keep both categories open: negotiate tax protection through relevant assessment periods plus a claims buffer, and tailored IP caps/survival**; tax exposure can outlast 18 months and core IP defects can undermine the business’s value. |

**Immediate priorities:** resolve Bluefen, Riverlark, bonus funding and Ironquay ownership before Completion; preserve separate recourse for disclosed risks rather than allowing disclosure or the general limitations package to extinguish it.
=== END ADVICE ===
